intent: Change and progress over ordered samples as a line or area chart.
useWhen: Following a trajectory across time or sequence
Parts of a total over time, like usage by plan by month — variant area with stack stacked
Each part's share of the total over time — variant area with stack percent
This period against the last — a second series with dashed true
Showing a target or average — referenceLine, with highlight to mark points past it
A headline value with how it moved each day — highlightLast with a changeStrip
This period against the last on demand — a Compare Button in actions that adds a dashed series
doNotUseWhen: Comparing unrelated magnitudes at one moment — use BarChart
Part-to-whole share at one moment — use PieChart

series.note: { label, data: number[], color?, dashed? }[]. dashed draws the series as a dashed line with no area fill and a dashed legend swatch, for a comparison such as the previous period; it still counts toward the value axis.

referenceLine.note: One dashed horizontal guide (text.muted) at value, with its label at the line's right end. The value axis widens to include it. highlight marks points of solid series above (or below) it with an accent dot (fill.brand); not with stack (the edges are running totals). The table gets a caption with the label and value, and each point's name says when it is past the line. Ignored with stack percent.

highlightLast.note: A dot and a value chip on the latest point of the first solid series, like today's MRR. Ignored with stack.

changeStrip.note: A short bar strip under the plot on the same labels, like net change per day. Bars go up from zero for gains and down for losses, square, in the first solid series' colour, on their own scale with two axis labels. It shares the crosshair and tooltip, adds a legend item and a table column, and joins each point's accessible name. format defaults to a signed compact number with a real minus sign (+1,200, −1,600).

stack.note: Only with variant area. stacked piles the series as bands from the bottom up, so the top edge is the total; percent scales each column to 100% so the bands show each series' share. Missing or negative values count as 0. Ignored with variant line, with a warning in development

curve.note: smooth rounds the line through every point (monotone: no overshoot above peaks or below dips); linear draws straight segments

error.note: When set, the plot is replaced by the kit's "Couldn't load" row (role=alert) with this message. Say what failed and that data is safe, like "Stripe didn't answer in time."

onRetry.note: Shows an outline Retry Button on the error row.

tickInterval.note: draw every Nth axis label; with neither tickInterval nor formatLabel, labels thin automatically only when they would overlap

formatLabel.note: (label, index) => string for the painted axis label; return '' to hide one (turns off automatic thinning). Table and accessible names keep the raw label

tooltipNote.note: (index) => string | undefined. One sentence under the tooltip rows for that sample, like "The largest drop in 30 days." Read with the tooltip; keep it short and plain.

animate.note: Lines draw in left to right and area fills fade in after when the chart first appears. Runs when the chart mounts; changing data on a mounted chart does not replay it. To replay (e.g. one chart per Tabs panel, or a range switcher), give the chart a key that changes with the data. Off under prefers-reduced-motion

actions.note: Kit Buttons in the chart header, before the Table toggle, like an icon-only Ask. ghost sm reads quietest. Setting it draws the frame even with no title.

requirements: The plot svg is role=group named by the title when it holds focusable points (role=img only when empty)
animate is decorative only: no motion under prefers-reduced-motion, and hover, focus, legend and table work during the entrance
referenceLine: the table caption names the label and value; a highlighted point's accessible name adds "(above <label>)" or "(below <label>)"
dashed series are told apart by their legend label, not by the dash alone
changeStrip values are in the tooltip, the table and each point's accessible name; up and down are told by the sign, not by colour
The highlightLast chip is decorative (aria-hidden); the value stays in the table and the point's name
error replaces the plot with a role=alert row; Retry is a real Button
tooltipNote is read with the tooltip (role=status)

doNot: Do not invent chart container cousins
Do not draw bars and a line on one chart from two charts — use ComboChart
Do not plot two numeric measures per item (x against y) — use ScatterChart
Do not stack series that can go negative; a stacked band starts where the one below ends, so a negative value has nowhere to go
Do not stack values that do not add up to a real total, like rates, averages or overlapping counts; use stack none
Do not set stack with variant line; stacking needs filled bands
Do not draw a reference line or threshold with a second flat series — use referenceLine
Do not overlay a second chart to show the previous period — use a dashed series
Do not use status colours for highlighted points; the accent dot means past the line, the label says which way
Do not wrap a chart in a Card only to get a header button — pass actions
Do not draw a change strip as a second chart under the first — use changeStrip so labels, crosshair and tooltip stay shared
Do not colour strip bars green and red; a loss is a negative bar and its sign says so
Do not keep the comparison series on by default when it is only context — put a Compare Button in actions
Do not round line ends; the kit draws square ends and joins
snippet:
<LineChart title="Weekly active users" variant="area" data={[{ label: 'Mon', value: 1240 }]} />

<LineChart
  title="Usage by plan"
  variant="area"
  stack="stacked"
  labels={['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar']}
  series={[
    { label: 'Free', data: [1200, 1350, 1410] },
    { label: 'Pro', data: [640, 720, 810] },
  ]}
/>

<LineChart
  title="Signups"
  variant="line"
  labels={["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4"]}
  series={[
    { label: "This period", data: [310, 352, 298, 401] },
    { label: "Previous period", data: [280, 300, 315, 330], dashed: true },
  ]}
  referenceLine={{ value: 350, label: "Goal", highlight: "above" }}
/>

<LineChart
  title="MRR"
  labels={days}
  series={[{ label: "MRR", data: mrr }]}
  referenceLine={{ value: 405000, label: "Target" }}
  highlightLast
  changeStrip={{ label: "Net change per day", data: netChange }}
  tooltipNote={(index) => (index === worstDay ? "The largest drop in 30 days." : undefined)}
/>
